page: Microsoft Azure F32-8ams_v7 is an x86_64 server instance running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The virtual machine provides 8 dedicated AMD EPYC 9V45 cores operating at a maximum clock speed of 4.5 GHz with a 1:1 physical-to-virtual core allocation. The hardware architecture incorporates 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache per core cluster, with support for AVX-512, AVX-VNNI, and hardware-accelerated cryptographic extensions like AES and SHA-NI. The instance is provisioned with 256 GB of system memory, yielding a substantial 32 GB of RAM per core.

The F32-8ams_v7 includes no local ephemeral storage and does not feature integrated GPU hardware, meaning all persistent data operations depend on network-attached storage volumes. Benchmark results indicate exceptional single-core processing throughput, with stress-ng single-core tests ranking in the top tier and single-threaded gzip compression achieving 40.69 GB/sec. Conversely, multi-threaded stress-ng throughput and large-block memory bandwidth (54.9 GB/sec read and 34.12 GB/sec write) fall in the middle tier. In LLM inference tests, lightweight 135M models reach 389.22 tokens/sec in text generation, but performance drops sharply on large 70B models due to the 8-core CPU constraint.

By constraining the core count to 8 while supplying 256 GB of RAM, the instance offers favorable cost efficiency for enterprise software licensed on a per-core basis that still demands substantial memory footprints. This configuration avoids the expense of high-core-count VMs when raw parallel compute is not the primary bottleneck. Ideal workloads include memory-resident databases such as Redis, large-scale caching services, data preprocessing pipelines, and specialized analytics tasks where memory density and high clock speeds take precedence over aggregate multi-core scaling.
description: Microsoft Azure F32-8ams_v7 is an x86_64 instance configured with 8 dedicated physical cores and 8 vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor clocked at up to 4.5 GHz. Paired with 256 GB of memory, it delivers an expansive 32 GB of RAM per core, making it well-suited for memory-intensive computations. The processor includes 32 MB of L3 cache alongside hardware support for AVX-512, VNNI, and cryptographic acceleration instructions. Benchmark evaluations show top-tier single-core compute and compression efficiency, alongside average multi-core and memory subsystem throughput. The instance includes no bundled local storage or integrated GPU accelerators, requiring reliance on remote storage solutions. This architecture offers balanced cost efficiency for memory-heavy operations by avoiding excess core licensing overhead while maintaining substantial memory capacity. It is tailored for in-memory databases, large caching layers, data processing, and enterprise application deployments requiring high memory-per-core ratios.
